t: Count Apples and Oranges — LEFT JOIN Boxes With Their Chests
o: Boxes holds one row per box: its own fruit counts plus an optional chest_id pointing into Chests, whose row contributes additional fruit to that box. We must output a single row with grand totals named apple_count and orange_count over all boxes including their chests. Walking Example 1: box 18 owns 4 apples and links chest 14 (20 apples), contributing 4 + 20 = 24 apples and 15 + 10 = 25 oranges; boxes 20 and 8 both link chest 6 (5 apples, 6 oranges) and each legitimately adds those contents; chest-less box 2 counts only its own 6 apples and 15 oranges. Summing everything yields 151 apples and 123 oranges. Relationally this is a LEFT JOIN from Boxes to Chests — left, because boxes without chests must survive — followed by NULL-safe addition and one global aggregation: an INNER JOIN would silently drop chest-less boxes like box 2, and adding raw joined columns poisons SUM with NULL unless wrapped in IFNULL/COALESCE.
k: LEFT JOIN keeps chest-less boxes; IFNULL/COALESCE turns their NULL chest counts into 0 before summing.
Several boxes may reference the same chest (chest 6 serves boxes 20 and 8), so chest contents are counted once PER referencing box — join first, aggregate last, never pre-deduplicate Chests.
The result is exactly one row, so there is no GROUP BY at all — plain aggregates over all joined rows.

a.n: Approach 1: LEFT JOIN with NULL-Safe Aggregation
a.i:
Join every box to its chest (if any), coalesce missing chest counts to zero, add per-row fruit totals, and sum across all rows. The SQL form is:

```sql
SELECT SUM(b.apple_count + IFNULL(c.apple_count, 0)) AS apple_count,
       SUM(b.orange_count + IFNULL(c.orange_count, 0)) AS orange_count
FROM Boxes b
LEFT JOIN Chests c ON b.chest_id = c.chest_id;
```

The pandas translation mirrors merge + fillna + sum, while the general-purpose-language versions materialize the join with a hash map keyed by chest_id before reducing. One pass over each table is optimal since every row must be inspected.
s: LEFT JOIN Chests onto Boxes on chest_id so every box survives the join.
Replace missing chest-side counts with 0 (IFNULL / COALESCE / fillna).
Per row, add box and chest counts for both fruits.
Aggregate the two sums into a single output row labeled apple_count and orange_count.
a.t: O(B + C) — each box row and each chest row is processed once (hash join)
a.sp: O(C) — the lookup structure holding chest rows

w: For SQL questions the declarative answer IS the expected optimal — write the three-line query and explain the join semantics. Pitfalls: using INNER JOIN and losing chest-less boxes such as box 2; forgetting IFNULL/COALESCE so a single NULL makes the entire SUM NULL; worrying about double-counting shared chests (each referencing box SHOULD add its own copy of the chest contents); and mislabeling output columns — they must be exactly apple_count and orange_count per the expected format. Edge cases: no box references any chest (totals equal plain box sums), referenced chests with zero fruit, and large counts needing 64-bit accumulation. Follow-ups: report per-box totals instead (GROUP BY box_id), or support chests nested inside other chests (recursive CTE to walk the containment chain).
